author: haiku
label: c2-seed-haiku-01
changes: Added a short Terms section defining warehouse, online feature store, materialization, registry, aliases, shadow, fallback and p99, for readers new to the stack.

Kept the nine numbered steps and their headings, and kept the same order and content, but expanded each step into what starts it, what data moves, where state lives, and what happens on failure, as the brief asks.
Split the request path into numbered sub-steps with the 30 ms feature timeout, the 6-hour freshness rule, the fallback, and the point where shadow enqueueing happens, so the 150 ms budget is visible.
Stated that the feature lookup reads features for both the active and shadow models in one call, and that shadow jobs are queued after the response so they add no latency.
Explained the 10% user split as a fixed-salt hash into 100 buckets so a user stays in or out.
Defined how the daily comparison computes error rate (skipped runs excluded and reported separately) and how the 7-day clock starts and resets, and noted that missing days never count as passing.
Made the feature check explicit at three points: instance load, shadow run, and alias switch.
Explained that each instance keeps the previous version in memory so rollback is a pointer swap that fits the 1-minute target, and named the registry outage as the main risk.
Kept the Product A/B decision open: step 7 marks where a live test would sit and says the plan does not assume either option.
Added an Open items section for gaps the brief leaves unset: the model time limit, fewer-than-20 results, and whether rollback needs approval.
Defined the terms the plan relies on: feature row, feature manifest, feature check, shadow share, fallback and TTL-style freshness, so a reader new to the stack can follow each step.

Fixed a contradiction: the request path said it keeps no state, yet the comparison joined against 'the active model's logged results from step 3'. The shadow job now carries the active version's 20 IDs and the record copies them, so the comparison needs no join.
Removed ambiguous cross-references. 'Step 5' in the request path meant the fallback, but the document also has a top-level Step 5. Request-path items are now named 'step 3, item N'.

Separated the two feature checks: the version-level check against the feature manifest (step 4) and the per-user check against the feature row (step 3, item 3). Step 3 item 3 now routes a failed check to the fallback.
Stated that the shadow job is queued for fallback responses too, and that a missing feature is recorded as a skip.
Stated that the registry itself refuses a switch without approval (step 8), not only that the step cannot run.
Clarified rollback to an older version: instances must download it first, so only rollback to 'previous' is a pure pointer change.
Added an open item: rollback re-runs the feature check, so a dropped feature could block the rollback that is most needed.
Added an open item for the popular-items list (what computes it, and what happens on failure), with the last-loaded-list behaviour marked as an assumption to confirm.
Simplified sentences throughout and kept the original structure: nine numbered steps, each with starts, data moves, state and on-failure, plus Open items. No live A/B choice was made.
Added a short "How the parts fit" overview before the terms, so a reader sees the whole system before the details.
Defined the plain-language terms the steps rely on: atomic write, message queue, and append-only. Expanded the shadow share definition to state the 100 buckets and the 0 to 9 split.
Changed "pointer", "swap" and "one atomic write" wording in the steps to plainer phrasing, with the meaning explained in the terms.
Named the step 3 sub-list explicitly so "item 5" and "item 6" are unambiguous, and reworded the request path bullets for a reader new to the system.
Reworded the step 4 and step 9 timing sentences to say what the 15-second poll means for the 1-minute rollback target.
Reworded the open items for clarity without changing any of them. The content and order of the steps are unchanged.
